title: Charles Farrow — Family & Biography
body_markdown:
# Charles Farrow (~1836–1884)

**Role:** Husband of Elizabeth Hannah Telfer
**Born:** ~1836
**Died:** December 1884 — Pneumonia

Charles Farrow married Elizabeth Hannah Telfer. The book narrative records his death as December 1884 from pneumonia — 32 years before Elizabeth's death in 1916. (The chapter header shows 1828–1876, but the narrative text is the authoritative source.)

Together they had a large family including Peter, John, Charles, Esther Hannah, Elizabeth, Margaret, Sarah, Edith, James, Robert, William, and Eva Agnes Farrow.

**Source:** *From the Borders to the Bush* — Chapter on Elizabeth Hannah Telfer

## Family Stories

Charles Farrow married Elizabeth Telfer and the couple settled at Finniss Point, where they were close neighbours of the Flavel uncles who looked out for the young Telfer generation. It was these same uncles who knew of the high esteem in which the Tarlee schoolmistress Caroline Masters was held, and who steered young John Telfer her way — a chain of connections that ran right through the Farrow household at Finniss Point. Charles also stood as a witness at his sister-in-law Jane's second marriage to Frederick Parker, alongside his niece Jane Farrow, at the Wesleyan Church in Kapunda on Christmas Day 1871.

*(From the Borders to the Bush, pp.93, 110)*
